*Part B - Data Frames and Conditional Statement*
*B1*
```{r}
students <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

students
```

*B2*
```{r}
str(students)
dim(students)
colnames(students)
summary(students)

```

*B3*
```{r}
students$average <- round((students$midterm + students$final) / 2, 1)
students$average
```

*B4*
```{r}
students$passed <- (students$average >= 70) & (students$attendance >= 75)
students$passed
```

*B5*
```{r}
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

students$standing
```

*B6*
```{r}
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}
print(sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify))
```

*Part C - rbind() and cbind()*
*C1*
```{r}
new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
new_students$average <- round((new_students$midterm + new_students$final) / 2, 1)
new_students$passed <- (new_students$average >= 70) & (new_students$attendance >= 75)
new_students$standing <- ifelse(new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

new_students
new_students$average
new_students$passed
new_students$standing
students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
```

*C2*
```{r}
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz = quiz)
print(class(students_all))
```

*C3*
```{r}
a <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
mean_row <- c(mean(students_all$midterm), mean(students_all$final))
a_with_mean <- rbind(a, mean = mean_row)
print(a_with_mean)
```

*C4*
```{r}
tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad),
  error = function(e) {
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)
```
Answer(C4): When data frames have mismatched column names or counts, rbind() throws an error because it strictly requires identical column structures to bind rows together. tryCatch() allows the code to handle this exception gracefully without crashing the entire script execution.

```{r}
```
